    42	
    43	\section{Key theorem forms}
    44	
    45	Let $S$ and $T$ be binary observables and let $\rho$ be a positive
    46	semidefinite operator of trace one.  We distinguish the raw operator distance
    47	from the distance between their associated binary projective measurements:
    48	\begin{align*}
    49	  \draw_\rho(S,T)^2
    50	    &:= \Re\tr\big((S-T)^\dagger(S-T)\rho\big), \\
    51	  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2
    52	    &:= \sum_{s\in\{+,-\}}
    53	      \Re\tr\big((P_S^s-P_T^s)^\dagger
    54	                       (P_S^s-P_T^s)\rho\big),
    55	  \qquad P_S^\pm := \frac{\Id\pm S}{2}.
    56	\end{align*}
    57	The normalization and correlation identities are
    58	\begin{align}
    59	  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2 &= \frac12\draw_\rho(S,T)^2,
    60	    \tag{normalization}\label{eq:normalization}\\
    61	  \draw_\rho(S,T)^2
    62	    &= 2-2\Re\tr(ST\rho),
    63	    \tag{raw correlation}\label{eq:raw-correlation}\\
    64	  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2
    65	    &= 1-\Re\tr(ST\rho).
    66	    \tag{binary correlation}\label{eq:binary-correlation}
    67	\end{align}
    68	Consequently, the conclusion delivered by the quantum linearity argument can
    69	be written either as
    70	\[
    71	  \mathbb E_a\dbin_{\rho'}(\mathcal A(a),A(a))^2\leq\delta
    72	\]
    73	or, equivalently, as
    74	\[
    75	  \mathbb E_a\draw_{\rho'}(\mathcal A(a),A(a))^2\leq2\delta.
    76	\]
    77	These are not equivalent to the same bound $\delta$ for the raw distance.%
    78	\footnote{The formal declarations are \leanid{binaryObservableEffect},
    79	\leanid{binaryObservableDistSq},
    80	\leanid{binaryObservableDistSq\_eq\_stateDepDistSq\_div\_two},
    81	\leanid{stateDepDistSq\_eq\_two\_sub\_two\_mul\_correlation}, and
    82	\leanid{binaryObservableDistSq\_eq\_one\_sub\_correlation} in
    83	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/BooleanFourier.lean}.}
    84	
    85	\section{The source calculation}
    86	
    87	Natarajan and Vidick define the distance between two POVMs by summing the
    88	squared state-dependent distances between corresponding square roots
    89	\cite[Section~3.1]{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  For projective measurements the
    90	square roots are the effects themselves.  In the binary case their calculation
    91	expands $P_S^\pm=(\Id\pm S)/2$ and obtains
    92	\[
    93	  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2
    94	    = 1-\frac12\tr_\rho(ST+TS)
    95	    = \frac12\tr_\rho((S-T)^2).
    96	  \tag{source equation (3)}
    97	\]
    98	This is equation~(3) at lines~903--910 of the in-repository source mirror.%
    99	\footnote{See
   100	\path{references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex}, lines~866--912.  The quantum
   101	linearity theorem and its Fourier--Naimark proof are at lines~1074--1112.}
   102	The next line identifies the final expression with the squared raw operator
   103	distance.  The operator-distance definition at lines~873--875 is printed with
   104	$\rho$ occurring twice,
   105	\[
   106	  \draw_\rho(S,T)^2 = \tr_\rho\big((S-T)^\dagger(S-T)\rho\big),
   107	  \qquad \tr_\rho(X) := \tr(\rho X),
   108	\]
   109	and we read the duplication as typographical, keeping the single $\rho$ of the
   110	definition of $\draw$ above.  Under that reading the squared raw operator
   111	distance is $\tr_\rho((S-T)^2)$ rather than one half of that quantity.  Thus
   112	the calculation through line~910 is correct and the equality on line~911 loses
   113	a factor of two.
   114	
   115	The Fourier--Naimark proof is consistent with the measurement normalization.
   116	It proves
   117	\[
   118	  \mathbb E_a\operatorname{CON}_{\rho'}(A(a),\mathcal A(a))
   119	  = \frac12+\frac12\mathbb E_{a,b}
   120	       \tr_\rho(A(a)A(b)A(a+b)).
   121	\]
   122	The hypothesis therefore makes the consistency deficit at most $\delta/2$.
   123	For binary projective measurements, the squared measurement distance is twice
   124	that deficit, giving the bound $\delta$ in the normalized convention and the
   125	bound $2\delta$ in the raw convention.
   126	
   127	\section{A four-point counterexample}
   128	
   129	The raw bound with constant $\delta$ is false.  Let
   130	$G=(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^2$, choose $r\in G\setminus\{0\}$, take the
   131	one-dimensional state $\rho=1$, and define scalar binary observables by
   132	\[
   133	  A(a)=\begin{cases}
   134	    -1,&a=r,\\
   135	     1,&a\neq r.
   136	  \end{cases}
   137	\]
   138	For the characters $\chi_u(a)=(-1)^{u\cdot a}$, the normalized Fourier
   139	coefficients satisfy
   140	\[
   141	  \widehat A(0)=\frac12,
   142	  \qquad
   143	  \widehat A(u)=-\frac12\chi_u(r)\quad(u\neq0).
   144	\]
   145	Their multiset is
   146	$\{\frac12,\frac12,\frac12,-\frac12\}$, and hence
   147	\[
   148	  \mathbb E_{a,b}A(a)A(b)A(a+b)
   149	    =\sum_u\widehat A(u)^3=\frac14.
   150	\]
   151	The correlation hypothesis therefore holds with $\delta=3/4$.
   152	
   153	Every scalar exact Boolean representation is one of the characters $\chi_u$,
   154	and its average raw distance from $A$ is
   155	\[
   156	  \mathbb E_a |A(a)-\chi_u(a)|^2
   157	    =2-2\widehat A(u)\geq1.
   158	\]
   159	Allowing an ancillary space does not reduce this lower bound.  Exact linearity
   160	and the binary-observable relations make the operators $\mathcal A(a)$ a
   161	commuting family of Hermitian involutions.  Their simultaneous spectral
   162	subspaces carry characters of $G$.  Evaluation in any density operator is
   163	therefore a convex combination of the scalar character correlations above, so
   164	the average raw distance remains at least $1$.  It cannot be at most
   165	$\delta=3/4$.  By~\eqref{eq:normalization}, the corresponding normalized
   166	distance has lower bound $1/2$, which is compatible with the provider's
   167	conclusion.

   171	The QPBT paper quotes the quantum linearity theorem at lines~711--725 of its
   172	Pauli-basis analysis and defers its proof to Natarajan and Vidick.%

   177	$\draw$ while retaining the bound $\delta$.  The formal theorem

   179	average over $u$ of \leanid{stateDepDistSq} by $\delta$, makes the same
   180	choice.  Thus both carry the false normalization exhibited by the
   181	counterexample.%
   182	\footnote{See
   183	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}, lines~124--132, and
   184	\leanid{exists\_exactly\_linear\_observables} together with
   185	\leanid{stateDepDistSq} in

   188	The Boolean Fourier foundation keeps the raw definition unchanged and adds the
   189	separately named normalized measurement distance together with
   190	equations~\eqref{eq:normalization}--\eqref{eq:binary-correlation}.  It does not
   191	advertise the current source-labelled theorem as proved.  The statement repair
   192	should change the conclusion either to normalized distance at most $\delta$ or

   194	time.%
   195	\footnote{The normalization investigation is tracked in
   196	\ghissue{124}; the source-facing statement repair is assigned to
   197	\ghissue{129}.}
   198	
   199	\section{Conclusion}
   200	
   201	The provider's binary-measurement calculation is correct through the factor
   202	$1/2$ in equation~(3), but its final identification with raw observable
   203	distance is incorrect.  The theorem proved by the Fourier--Naimark argument has
   204	normalized binary-measurement error at most $\delta$, equivalently raw
   205	operator error at most $2\delta$.  The four-point example rules out the current
   206	raw-error bound $\delta$ even when arbitrary ancillary extensions are allowed.

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (changes) `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex:188` — The formalization comparison omits `exists_exact_boolean_representation` and its essential reparameterization `η = 2δ`.
- [ ] F2 (changes) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:196` — The remark attributes an exact raw-distance bound by `δ` to the QPBT quotation, although that paper defines `≈_δ` only up to `O(δ)`.
- [ ] F3 (advisory) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Stability.lean:255` — The new public stability theorem has no blueprint declaration link or dedicated corrected-theorem entry.

## Review

F1 must be fixed before merge. The paper-gap policy requires the note to state what the formal development proves instead. The note currently says only that the Fourier foundation adds normalization identities and that theorem repair remains future work. This PR also proves `avg_stateDepDistSq_roundedObservable_eq_avg_multiplicativeDefect` and `exists_exact_boolean_representation`. Their relationship to the source parameter is material: the identity
\[
\mathbb E_{a,b}d_\rho(A(a)A(b),A(a+b))^2=2-2C
\]
turns the source hypothesis \(C\geq1-\delta\) into the new theorem’s hypothesis with \(\eta=2\delta\), yielding raw output error at most \(2\delta\). The note, and the theorem docstring at `Stability.lean:245`, should identify this as the corrected raw-distance reformulation rather than simply calling it Theorem 10.

F2 must also be fixed. The QPBT source defines `≈_δ` at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:95-99` as an expectation bounded by `O(δ)` and uses that notation in `thm:linearity` at lines 713–725. A factor of two is absorbed there.
